newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent slumps, other N.Sea grades active.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent slumps, other N.Sea grades active.

text.p: Dated Brent slumped further on Thursday on an overhang of prompt cargoes although other North Sea grades were active with differentials holding firm as refiners rushed to cover requirements.
One of the two Brent cargoes which turned wet on Thursday was clocked and in dispute, raising the possibility yet another homeless Brent cargo would drift into the market and depress prices further.
An equity producer offered a Sept 13-15 loading Brent late at October -5 cents after earlier buying a cargo from a trader at October evens.
The same company has picked up Brent cargoes in recent days, suggesting the North Sea benchmark would be moving transatlantic once the arbitrage window opened again.
"We are trying to work the arb. If it opens, we will move it there," the trader said. He added that the Brent/WTI spread had come in to $1.30 on Monday from $1.40 on Friday.
Another oil major was also seen holding one million barrels of Brent and reports the cargo was sold could not be confirmed.
The most active grade was Forties, with more than two million barrels loading in second half Sept trading at Dated Brent +35 cts and =37 cts, the latter slightly up on last deals.
An Ekofisk loading September 28 was done at Dated +35 cents and a Sept 20 Gullfaks was sold at Dated +18 cents, both differentials holding steady despite Brent's predicament.
No paper deals were heard done on Thursday.
In West Africa, two or three prompt Escravos cargoes were on offer, with differentials pegged at a steady Dated Brent +30/35.
Two Qua Iboe cargoes and one Brass River were also available in September, but traders said that buying interest was slack.
"The remaining September barrels are struggling," said one dealer.
